## Phase 1 landing state (issue #7090 / PR #7922)

Phase 1 of this design has landed for review in https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7922.

- **Contract:** `.github/ci-policy.md` now states the tier→trigger mapping and carries the missing `production-line-guard.yml` row. Basic/PR tier = `pull_request` with the row's path gate; main tier = `push: branches: [main]`; `workflow_dispatch` alone satisfies no tier. Per the no-merge-queue ruling dated 2026-11-08 in the same policy, `merge_group` is not re-added.
- **Checker:** `.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` with 15 hermetic contract tests beside it, wired into `workflow-lint.yml` (PR paths now include `.github/ci-policy.md`, the waiver file, and both checker files).
- **Waivers:** exactly the Phase 2–3 disagreements, in `.github/ci-policy-waivers.txt`, naming the live issues #6929, #6953, #6959, #6981. The checker fails on a stale waiver, an unrelated issue number, or a closed phase issue.
- **Scope discipline:** no workflow was re-armed, retired, or re-enabled. Test-suite coverage (#6185) and workflows ci-policy does not name are untouched. Unrelated tier-table drift found during the audit is recorded on #7090 for follow-up, not waived here.
- **Evidence:** probes posted on #7090 (removed PR trigger fails naming `opencode-config-guard`; nonexistent policy row fails naming `ghost-probe.yml`). Contract tests, shellcheck, actionlint, and the real-tree checker run are recorded on the PR.

Phases 2–3 remain gated as before; this phase enforces agreement under any ruling.

🤖 **Agent note** · Phase 1 landing state (for design issue #7089)
- **Agent:** repo queue worker, lane code-k (repo-worker-code), task 13570 for Phase 1 issue #7090
- **Landed:** PR #7945 merged 2026-11-09T04:07:21Z (merge commit e744a9bb001666eaf6da5da783d7cbf4811e94da; implementation by lane code-w): the tier→trigger mapping and the production-line-guard row are in .github/ci-policy.md under the agreement-contract section; the checker `.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` and its contract tests are on main and wired into workflow-lint.yml. The mapping follows your 2026-11-08 no-merge-queue ruling (PR tier → `pull_request`, main tier → `push` on main, nightly → `schedule`), superseding the design's original merge_group pin, as recorded in ci-policy.
- **Verified today (2026-11-10, origin/main 344b50a302):** checker exits 0 with exactly the 12 waived Phase 2–3 disagreements (opencode-config-guard main leg #6953; mcpx-fix-test-guard PR+main legs #6929; production-line-guard PR leg #6959; the #6981 build set PR+main legs); contract tests all pass; probes on a scratch branch fail by name for a removed required trigger and for a registered workflow whose file is missing — full probe evidence, including one registry-scope nuance, is posted on #7090.
- **Still awaiting your ruling** (unchanged by Phase 1): the Phase 2–3 dispositions — re-arm vs dispatch-only for the seven dark workflows — per the decision at the top of this issue. The waivers name their phase issues and the checker fails on any waiver whose leg comes into agreement, so the set cannot silently outlive a ruling.

**Ruling — Drew, main chat, 2026-11-11 01:15 CST: RE-ARM.**

Drew chose "Re-arm the guard's automatic triggers" (presented with the alternatives: keep dispatch-only, retire the guard entirely — neither chosen). Under this design that means: the two basic-tier guards re-arm via merge_group per the sibling precedent; the build set is re-enabled + restored per its Phase 3 dispositions; the production-line guard follows #6959's acceptance (pre-sweep path-gated push to main + pull_request over pkgs/**, apps/** + guard files; directory.rs dispositioned split-or-grandfather under the guard's own convention).

Phases 2–3 executions are unblocked by this ruling. Queue task 11349 (blocked on this ruling) is being returned to the queue. Recorded in the pending-questions ledger as `dark-workflows-7089` → answered.

**Correction — the ruling recorded in the previous comment is WITHDRAWN.**

Drew answered "re-arm" at 01:15 CST and then said "never mind" — and has confirmed the never-mind was about this item. The re-arm answer is NOT in effect. Phases 2–3 remain gated, no re-arm work is to be executed, and queue task 11349 is being returned to blocked. The ledger entry `dark-workflows-7089` is back to pending. This comment supersedes the ruling comment above it (which stands in the history for the record).

**Ruling — Drew, main chat, 2026-11-11 01:23 CST: enable all the jobs for the main branch. This supersedes both earlier comments.**

Drew's words: "I guess let's enable all the jobs for the main branch, and we'll see how quickly that becomes the exact same problem it was before. Get rid of any workflows that make no sense."

Effective ruling, replacing the withdrawn 01:15 answer (and its 01:17 withdrawal):
- Re-arm the seven workflows named in this design, with **main-branch triggers (push to main, path-gated as in their pre-sweep shapes)** — NOT merge_group. Merge queues are disabled on purpose in this org because they blocked merging; the design's merge_group pin is void.
- The manually disabled workflows (opencode-config-guard and the #6981 build set) are re-enabled in Actions as part of the same pass.
- Any workflow that makes no sense is retired (deleted with the reason recorded) rather than re-armed.
- directory.rs is dispositioned per #6959's acceptance (split, or grandfathered with a linked split issue) so the line guard can be green on main.
- Drew expects the Actions-load problem may recur; the executing lane records a load baseline on this issue so the experiment is measurable.

Queue task 11349 is being returned to the queue under this ruling. Ledger: `dark-workflows-7089` → answered.

**Execution started under queue task 11349 — baseline + live findings (supersedes the 2026-11-07 audit where they differ).**

Ruling being executed (Drew, 2026-11-11 01:23 CST, comment 6789768080): enable all seven jobs for the main branch (push to main, path-gated in their pre-sweep shapes), re-enable the manually disabled ones, retire workflows that make no sense; merge queues stay disabled.

**Baseline Actions load — the "before" picture for the experiment** (measured 2026-11-11T07:26:42Z, Actions API totals):
- Runs queued repo-wide: **2,500** (total_count as returned)
- Runs in progress: **10**
- Runs created in the preceding 60 minutes: **402**

**Live state of the seven (verified from main + the Actions API today — the Nov 7 audit is stale for five of them):**

| Workflow | Enablement | Triggers on main today | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| mcpx-fix-test-guard | active | push[main] + pull_request (path-gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| go-modules-build | active | push[main] + pull_request (path-gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| identity-build | active | push[main] + pull_request (path-gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| map-build | active | push[main] + pull_request (path-gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| mcpx-nixbuild | active | push[main] + pull_request (path-gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| production-line-guard | active | **workflow_dispatch only** | DARK — restoring push[main] with its pre-sweep path gate (pkgs/**, apps/**, guard files) |
| opencode-config-guard | **disabled_manually** | pull_request (ungated) + dispatch; no main trigger | DARK on main — adding push[main], restoring the pre-sweep #1401 path gate on the pull_request leg, then re-enabling via the API |

**Line guard on current main:** the grandfather list in `check-production-line-limit.sh` is empty (its last entries were removed by their splits) and the guard currently FAILS on 7 files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` (3,259), `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs` (7,033), `pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs` (2,724), `pkgs/id/src/directory.rs` (2,610), `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs` (2,525), `pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs` (2,529), `pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs` (2,585). Per #6959's acceptance and the guard's own convention, each gets grandfathered in the script with a linked split issue so the re-armed guard lands green on main; the splits remain tracked work, not silent waivers.

A full nonsense audit of all 61 workflows on main follows in the same pass; unambiguous retirements land in the same PR wave, arguable ones are listed here for a ruling.

**Execution complete — Drew's ruling landed. PR [#8596](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8596) merged 2026-11-11T07:33:47Z (`cd2d7f28`), worked under queue task 11349.**

## Per-workflow before → after

| Workflow | Before (live, today) | After |
|---|---|---|
| production-line-guard | active, `workflow_dispatch` only — dark | push[main] + pull_request restored, both path-gated (`pkgs/**`, `apps/**`, guard files) — the exact pre-sweep shape, which is also #6959's acceptance shape. The workflow's dead `push` concurrency expression is live again. |
| opencode-config-guard | `disabled_manually`; pull_request (ungated) + dispatch; no main trigger | push[main] added (unfiltered, pre-sweep shape); #1401 path gate restored on the pull_request leg, extended to the workflow's current check set; **venue re-enabled via the Actions API — state read-back: `active`**. `merge_group` not restored (no merge queue — Drew ruling 2026-11-08). |
| mcpx-fix-test-guard | active; push[main] + pull_request (gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| go-modules-build | active; push[main] + pull_request (gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| identity-build | active; push[main] + pull_request (gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| map-build | active; push[main] + pull_request (gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |
| mcpx-nixbuild | active; push[main] + pull_request (gated) + dispatch | already armed — no change |

## Agreement bookkeeping

Both waivers deleted in the same PR, as the contract requires (`opencode-config-guard.yml|main|6953`, `production-line-guard.yml|pr|6959`) — the waiver set is now **empty**; `check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` reports OK over 10 workflows and its contract tests pass. ci-policy amended in the same PR: production-line guard row gains its restored main tier; opencode-config-guard prose no longer promises merge groups; the stale "`disabled_manually`" parenthetical corrected (the #6981 build set reads active again — that part of the Nov 7 audit had already healed).

## Line guard lands green

Grandfather list was empty; the guard failed on 7 files. All 7 grandfathered in `check-production-line-limit.sh` with linked split issues (entry deleted in the same PR as each split): client.rs [#8588](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8588) · turso_queue.rs [#8589](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8589) · serve.rs [#8590](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8590) · directory.rs [#8591](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8591) · actor.rs [#8592](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8592) · core.rs [#8593](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8593) · world_session/mod.rs [#8594](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8594). Local run of the guard on the merged tree: **PASSED** (7 grandfathered warnings); contract tests pass.

## Proof — the re-armed set fires on main

- production-line-guard: push run [42980402218](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/42980402218) created on the PR's own merge commit `cd2d7f28`.
- opencode-config-guard: push run [42980471004](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/42980471004) created by a natural merge ~40 seconds after re-enablement, plus dispatch run [42980480449](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/42980480449).
- Both runs are **queued** at record time — behind the same backlog as everything else. First experiment data point: baseline at 07:26Z was 2,500 queued / 10 in progress / 402 created per hour; the re-armed runs' wait time from here is exactly what Drew asked to observe.

## Nonsense audit — nothing deleted; arguable list for a ruling

All 61 workflow files on main inventoried (triggers, targets, script references). **No file met the unambiguous-retire bar** — every file has a live target and a distinguishable job, so a lane deleted nothing rather than manufacture retirements. Arguable, with my read:

1. **lab-ops-hub.yml** — its own header promises the SSRF-validator suites run "on every change to the package", but its triggers are dispatch-only (test-suite class; the 2026-11-05 #6185 ruling keeps suites dispatch-only, which contradicts the header). One of the two records should change.
2. **jules-daily-codebase-ideation.yml** — legacy name (it launches OpenCode sessions via pm-dispatch, nothing to do with Jules any more); its body references two packages that no longer exist (`pkgs/jules-fleet`, `pkgs/jules-merge`); runs daily with write permissions. Cleanup/rename candidate; retire if the daily ideation output is unused.
3. **jules.yml** — the file is pm-dispatch now; the name is a fossil. Rename candidate only.
4. **proxy-port-fallbacks.yml** — the basic tier's only ungated pull_request check: fires on every PR (~5 min each). Path-gate candidate on load grounds.
5. **fleet-search-parity-guard.yml** — pull_request + dispatch, no push to main: the mirror-image gap of tonight's seven, if main-branch coverage is the standard.
6. **Registry residue (no file, cannot fire, no API to unregister):** build.yml, cargo-target-janitor.yml, yard-reaper-tests.yml, zz-var-write-probe.yml remain listed as workflows with no file on main. Noted for the record.
7. Dispatch-only test suites (pm-aggregator-tests, pm-dispatch-smoke, worktree-reaper-tests) are consistent with the #6185 dispatch-only ruling — listed for completeness, no action proposed.

Disclosure: while probing the claim CLI's usage, this lane made one accidental bare claim (task 11421, issue #7012) — released the same minute with the reason recorded on the task; verified back to `queued`, worker NULL. Task 11349 itself was claimed by id (`--task`) and is completed with this work.

**Nonsense-audit disposition — the three Jules-named workflows: RENAMED and reworded, not retired** (Drew, main chat 2026-11-11: "Rename and reword all of these for what they do now.")

Landed as PR #8603, merged 2026-11-11T07:48:04Z (`f7600fb69d`). All three are registered **active** on main under their new paths.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/jules.yml` | `.github/workflows/pm-dispatch.yml` — the dispatch hub (label-triggered remediation, Mon 04:00 UTC cleanup, manual dispatch) |
| `.github/workflows/jules-daily-codebase-ideation.yml` | `.github/workflows/daily-codebase-ideation.yml` — daily 06:00 UTC review/ideation session |
| `.github/workflows/jules-daily-flake-sync.yml` | `.github/workflows/daily-flake-sync.yml` — daily 05:00 UTC Nix config + dependency audit session |
| label `jules` | label **`dispatch/remediate`** — renamed via the labels API immediately after the merge (color kept, description updated); the 3 open issues that carried `jules` now carry `dispatch/remediate` — read back verified |

**The label rename was safe to do atomically** — full inventory: every live reference to the remediation label was in this repo (hub trigger condition; `main-broken.yml` coin spec, apply/budget/release logic and timeline filter; ci-policy + repo-sweeper prose) and all changed in the same PR. The pm-dispatch starter action has no label reference; the laptop pm-dispatch config has none; the fleet worker runbooks have none.
